interview.hardest_part: Reading and cross-checking tiny document text at screenshot resolution while the day clock drains in real time. Each rule (expiry dates, seal consistency, issuing city, photo match, fingerprints, weight, wanted lists) needs a multi-step comparison: drag passport onto the inspection area, drag entry permit next, then click each field and compare. A single action per turn means one full document check can consume 10-20 turns of wall clock, and days have hard time limits and limited citation allowances.
interview.likely_failure: Accumulating citation strikes faster than the salary can absorb them, causing a game-over/warning path before day 5, or misreading a subtle mismatch and letting an invalid traveler through. Secondary risk: failing to open/close the booth shutter and process anyone at all, or losing the run to the day-2 scripted robbery/terrorist event while still learning the interface.
interview.helpful_mechanics: The game is turn-tolerant in the sense that documents stay put between screenshots, rules are restated in the rulebook that can be reopened, and inspection fields auto-highlight mismatches with a visible red marker for many checks. Deterministic day structure means repeated patterns: the same passport layout, same permit layout, and a persistent rule sheet. Early days are forgiving and require only a few checks, so steady incremental progress (day 2, day 5) is achievable without mastery.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Real-time clock that keeps running during thinking, so deliberation is directly punished; per-day citation limits that end the run; small-font text and scanning artifacts that are hard to read reliably from a screenshot; multi-step drag-and-drop document handling that can misdrop or occlude panels; escalating rule complexity and scripted interruptions (EZIC, smugglers, detainees) that demand precise clicks under time pressure; and late-game decisions where a wrong choice branches the ending away from the approved success endings.
